samples.reason: This is a math-heavy design-and-solve task requiring careful number-theoretic reasoning (constructing a modulus from a Pythagorean-style difference of squares, running the extended Euclidean algorithm correctly). Dunlin's substantially stronger reasoning benchmarks (MMLU-Pro 81.2 vs 75.9, GPQA 64.1 vs 56.2) matter most here for getting the arithmetic and construction right. This is an open-ended math construction task requiring careful number-theoretic reasoning (choosing a modulus that factors via a difference of squares from a Pythagorean-style triple, verifying coprimality, executing the extended Euclidean algorithm correctly). Dunlin is meaningfully stronger on reasoning-heavy benchmarks (GPQA 64.1 vs 56.2, MMLU-Pro 81.2 vs 75.9), which matters most for getting the arithmetic and construction right. It also avoids handing a high-latitude, "design it yourself" task to Willet, which self-reports aversion to open-ended generative work.
